oracle.reference: tests/conformance/data expected JSON (16 variants supported by CppIndexedReaderTestRunner, compared with a Python re-implementation of run-tests/index.ts expectedResult + json-stable-stringify); pristine cpp/test/unit_tests.cpp (18/16 Catch2 cases on Linux; one case is #if __linux__); 14 generated fixtures (tests/harness/gen_fixtures.py, a self-contained MCAP writer that records ground truth) driven through a hidden probe (tests/harness/indexed_probe.cpp) compiled against the submission: 42 readSummary/byteRange checks + 157 readMessages queries; Go indexed reader (tests/harness/go_indexed_reader.go = upstream test-read-conformance readIndexed with a nil-schema guard, built with go build -overlay against the pristine go/mcap) and Rust conformance_indexed_reader built in the verifier image must match the C++ LogTimeOrder output on 9 fixtures (18 comparisons)
oracle.comparison_semantics: corpus: structural JSON equality after key-sorted serialization, message order significant, all scalars strings (identical to the TS harness); fixtures: exact message tuples (channel, sequence, log/publish time, payload, and for index-based reads offset+chunk offset), exact status codes, set-equality of distinct problem codes; siblings: (channel, payload, log_time, publish_time, sequence) sequences, strict across distinct log_time values and as multisets within runs of equal log_time (Go orders cross-chunk ties by chunk load order, C++/Rust by offset; the spec leaves it open, and the C++ offset tie-break is asserted exactly by the fixture queries)
oracle.ts_harness_decision: Not vendored. The TypeScript harness needs Yarn 4 workspaces and a built @mcap/core; its comparison logic for indexed readers is ~60 lines (dedupe schemas/channels by id, stable-sort messages by log_time, stable stringify) and was re-implemented in tests/harness/conformance_compare.py, validated to accept the pristine runner on all 16 variants and reject the excised one on all 16.

contamination.notes: The excised code is public in foxglove/mcap history and in Conan Center releases of mcap 2.x. The agent tree also contains the Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript and Swift readers, which implement the same behaviour (Go indexed_message_iterator.go, Rust sans_io/indexed_reader.rs, Python _message_queue.py); porting from them is possible but the C++ contract (MissingStatistics retention, fallback-scan synthesis, byteRange, RecordOffset conventions, iterator integration, ReadJobQueue API) still has to be reconstructed. No .git history is shipped. Interface not shifted in this phase.
